title: UnDercontrol RecurringExpense Resource
description: Schema for recurring expense YAML resource files. A recurring expense is the PLAN of a series of payments (a subscription, a phone contract, an installment): what it costs per period, how often, until when, and how long it is locked in. It is not money spent and never counts toward a total. Each real payment is an ordinary Expense whose spec.recurring_expense_id points back at the plan, and spec.recurring_periods says how many periods it settles. Periods are never stored: due, settled and pending counts are derived on every read (spec.schedule). Subscription, contract and installment are not a field: they are which of ends_at and committed_until are set.

name.description: What this plan is (e.g., 'Acme Mobile phone contract', 'Netflix').

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency of every amount in the plan (e.g., SGD, USD, CNY).

starts_at.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) the plan starts, e.g. the contract signing day.

first_due.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the first payment. Later due dates step from here by frequency; a day past the end of a month is clamped to its last day.

terms.description: Price segments, each the per-period amount from effective_from (inclusive) until effective_to or the next segment; a day no segment covers costs 0. A price change is a new segment, not an edit. On update the whole list is replaced.

ends_at.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD): the last day covered, not the last payment date; every period starting on or before this day counts. A plan billed in arrears is therefore paid once more after it. Omit for an open-ended subscription. On update, "" clears it.

committed_until.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD): the last day of the contract lock-in; every period starting on or before this day is locked in, and leaving earlier costs exit_fee. Omit when you can cancel any time. On update, "" clears it.

default_budget_id.description: Budget UUID a payment of this plan is usually booked to. Only prefills a new payment; it is not a link.

default_pay_account.description: Account UUID a payment of this plan is usually paid from. Only prefills a new payment.

possession_id.description: Possession UUID this plan belongs to (the phone a contract came with). One possession can carry several plans.

status.description: active, or ended. A new plan is always active. Applying status: ended with ended_at and end_reason to an active plan ends it (unsubscribed, paid off, terminated early); an ended plan cannot be reopened.

ended_at.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) the plan ended. Required with status: ended; no period starting after it is due.

end_reason.description: Why the plan ended: completed (paid off / ran its course), cancelled (unsubscribed), terminated_early (left a lock-in, exit fee due). Required with status: ended.

owner_id.description: User UUID that owns the plan.

group_id.description: Group UUID the plan is shared to, if any. Sharing is its own channel, not part of the apply document.

attention.description: Why the plan deserves a look as of schedule.as_of: periods not yet recorded, a price change within 30 days (ignored when under 1.00 per month and under 5%), a renewal, the end of the lock-in, the end of the plan. Empty when nothing needs a look.

payments.description: The expenses that point at this plan, as the detail view shows them. Only on a single-plan read.

amount.description: Per-period amount in major units of spec.currency (44.90).

effective_from.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) this price applies from. A period costs the price in force on the day it STARTS (starts_at plus n periods), not on its due date: with starts_at 2027-01-08 and first_due 2027-02-08, the period due 2027-02-08 started 2027-01-08.

effective_to.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) this price applies until. Omit to run until the next segment or forever.

reason.description: Why the price is what it is (e.g., 'promo ends').

exit_fee.description: What leaving before committed_until costs. Nothing after committed_until. On update, an empty mode clears the rule.

base.description: Amount in major units of spec.currency the mode works from.

mode.description: fixed: base, whenever you leave. prorata_remaining: base scaled by the share of locked-in periods still to come. remaining_payments: the sum of the locked-in periods still to come (base unused).

schedule.description: Derived on every read, never stored. Amounts in major units of spec.currency.

as_of.description: The calendar day these figures are for (YYYY-MM-DD).

due_count.description: Periods due on or before as_of.

settled_count.description: Sum of recurring_periods of the visible expenses that point at the plan.

pending_count.description: due_count minus settled_count, never below 0: periods not recorded yet.

pending_since.description: Due date of the oldest pending period.

settled_expected_amount.description: What the settled periods were expected to cost ...

paid_amount.description: ... next to what the linked expenses actually paid.

current_amount.description: Per-period price in force as of as_of.

next_due_date.description: Equal to last_due_date when the next period is the plan's last one.

exit_cost_today.description: What leaving on as_of would cost under exit_fee.

total_periods.description: All periods of a plan with an end (ends_at, or ended). Absent when the plan has no end. A plan ended as completed or terminated_early has no period due after its end day; one ended as cancelled still bills a period that had already started.

last_due_date.description: Due date of the plan's last period. Absent when the plan has no end or no period at all.
